SLA / SA Caches

The SA / SLA toolchain keeps several caches. Most of them key on file contents only — not on the compiler or plugin version — so after a compiler or plugin rebuild, a stale cache silently replays artefacts produced by the old compiler. The symptoms lie in both directions: a real fix looks as if it did nothing, or a healthy tree looks broken.

This chapter has two parts: the first half is diagnosis and workarounds for the current state (location, key, symptoms, cleanup); the second half is a root-fix roadmap — making the toolchain itself decide whether a cache is stale, instead of relying on human judgement. Once a root fix lands, the corresponding workaround text can be deleted (see "Maintenance conventions").

Rule: before verifying any compiler or plugin change, clear all six cache surfaces below. When a gate or canary result contradicts the state of the tree, clearing caches is the first step of the investigation, not the last resort. Clearing is always safe — every cache regenerates; the only cost is rebuild time.

Symptom lookup

Locate the row by symptom first, then see the matching row of the table below. When several symptoms appear together, clear everything per the cleanup checklist.

SymptomCheck first
A fixed compiler still crashes the same way or reports the same error#1 macro index, #2 frontend cache, #5 freshness cache
Plugin source changed, behaviour completely unchangedTrap "dev mode loads the installed plugin", trap "install swallows build errors", #2
The same test file keeps failing, while a byte-identical copy passes elsewhere#4 sa test artefact cache
Canary / gate reports red on a healthy tree#6 project / demo directory artefact cache
zig build exits in 0 seconds and rebuilds nothing; the .so is about 129 MB#3 build-graph cache (a Debug configuration was remembered)
zig build test returns rc=0 but the log is emptyTrap "zig build test caches successful runs"
sa_std/*.sa changed, static library behaviour unchangedTrap "sa-std-static archive freshness"

The six cache surfaces

The "Status" column: manual means the surface still has to be cleared per this table; once a root fix lands it becomes fixed (version).

#CacheLocationKeyFailure modeCleanupStatus
1SLA macro index cache.sla-cache/ inside the sa_plugin_sla tree (macros/*.idx)Macro file path + length + source hash; no compiler analysis version After a compiler change it still replays old macro expansions; a fixed compiler keeps crashing or erroring in exactly the same way. Delete the tree's .sla-cache. Note: SLA_NO_FRESHNESS_CACHE=1 does not cover this cache.manual
2Host frontend cacheDefault ~/.cache/sa/frontend. Resolution order (verified against the current sci source, frontendCacheRoot in broker_runtime.zig): SA_FRONTEND_CACHE_DIR overrides the root outright, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME/sa/frontend, then $HOME/.cache/sa/frontend Source file sha256 only; no plugin / compiler versionAfter a plugin rebuild, compiling an unchanged .sla replays the first compilation's output; a fix can look completely ineffective for several rounds in a row.Delete the resolved cache root (default ~/.cache/sa/frontend; on machines that set the two variables above, delete the resolved root).manual
3Build-graph cache.zig-cache/ and zig-out/ inside the plugin tree The Zig build graph, including the optimisation mode captured at configuration time If the environment carries SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 during a build or install, the build graph remembers a Debug configuration: the plugin .so balloons (about 129 MB, vs about 37 MB for ReleaseFast), and a later plain zig build exits in 0 seconds and rebuilds nothing. Delete both .zig-cache and zig-out (deleting only one is not enough), and build / install with env -u SA_PLUGIN_DEV. Running still needs SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 — the build and run environments differ.manual
4sa test artefact cache.sa_cache/test/<hash>/artifact.sa.bc inside each test directory Test source hash; no compiler version sa test replays bitcode built by the old compiler; the same test file keeps failing or crashing because of its own cache, while a byte-identical copy passes elsewhere. Delete .sa_cache in the affected test directories.manual
5Standalone CLI freshness cache.sla-cache/fresh/ under the working directory ({stem}-{key}.bin artefacts + .json manifests; verified against the current sla-cli source, freshness.rs) File path + compile-options digest + a version stamp (a cache-key version constant + the crate version); no build identity — a rebuild under the same version number is not distinguished The compile pipeline returns the cached .sa and skips the frontend entirely; new compiler behaviour never runs.Delete .sla-cache/fresh/ in the project directory, or run with SLA_NO_FRESHNESS_CACHE=1. That variable covers only this one surface — despite the global-sounding name, it reaches none of #1–#4 or #6.manual
6Project / demo directory artefact cache.sa_cache/ inside demo and project directories (the same store as #4, in a different place; possibly outside the plugin tree)Same as #4 build-exe replays a stale artifact.sa.bc left by the old compiler — it once made a canary cell on a healthy tree report false red for a whole day. Before a canary or gate run, delete .sa_cache in the demo / project directories.manual

Cleanup checklist

Run in order. Scanning only the plugin tree misses .sa_cache in demo / project directories outside it (#6), and the rebuild must drop SA_PLUGIN_DEV (#3); the checklist below covers both.

# 0. Adjust the paths for your machine
PLUGIN="<path to the sa_plugin_sla tree>"
ROOTS=("$PLUGIN" "<demo root>" "<project root>")   # every root that may contain .sa_cache

# 1. Plugin tree: macro index + build graph (#1 #3)
rm -rf "$PLUGIN/.sla-cache" "$PLUGIN/.zig-cache" "$PLUGIN/zig-out"

# 2. Host frontend cache (#2): default path below; on machines that set
#    XDG_CACHE_HOME / SA_FRONTEND_CACHE_DIR, delete the resolved root instead
rm -rf ~/.cache/sa/frontend

# 3. All artefact caches (#4 #6) — scan outside the plugin tree too
for r in "${ROOTS[@]}"; do
  find "$r" -type d -name .sa_cache -prune -exec rm -rf {} +
done

# 4. Rebuild and install: drop SA_PLUGIN_DEV from the build environment (#3)
(cd "$PLUGIN" && env -u SA_PLUGIN_DEV sa plugin install --dev .)

# 5. Install confirmation (see trap 1 below): the installed .so's mtime / size changed,
#    and a string literal newly introduced this round greps in the .so
ls -l "$HOME/.local/share/sa_plugins/installed/"
grep -c "<string introduced this round>" "$HOME/.local/share/sa_plugins/installed/<plugin .so>"

# 6. Run: the run environment needs SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1; the standalone CLI also takes the freshness switch (#5)
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 SLA_NO_FRESHNESS_CACHE=1 <your command>

Same-family traps (silent staleness, not cache surfaces)

The traps below are not cache surfaces, but the symptoms are the same. The "Root fix" at the end of each item is a proposal, not implemented.

  • sa plugin install --dev swallows build errors. On a build failure it can exit 0 and keep the old .so. After installing, always double-confirm: the installed .so's mtime / size changed, and a string literal newly introduced this round greps in the .so. Take md5 only after the install has settled, and compare it only within the same build → install round: plugin .so bytes are not reproducible across rebuilds, so a cross-round md5 comparison is meaningless. On a new machine the bare form may also demand an explicit path: sa plugin install --dev .
    Root fix: return a non-zero exit code and refuse to install on build failure; add sa plugin info showing the installed plugin's build-id, replacing md5 / grep checks.
  • Dev mode loads the installed plugin, not the working tree. sa sla check / test run the plugin under $HOME/.local/share/sa_plugins/installed/; editing sources in the tree plus zig build changes no behaviour at all. Any A/B comparison must first install the tree under test into that round's HOME and md5-check the installed .so.
    Root fix: warn at startup when the installed plugin does not match the current working tree; offer a flag to load the plugin straight from the working tree.
  • zig build test caches successful runs. A previously successful round is silently replayed (rc=0, empty log, shown as run test cached under --summary all); failures are not cached, which makes this trap easy to miss. Judging rules are in "Judging a run" below.
    Root fix: mark the test step as having side effects in build.zig so it really runs every time to verify the exact API depends on the project's Zig version.
  • sa-std-static archive freshness. zig build sa-std-static does not track sa_std/*.sa as step inputs, so a warm rebuild can replay the old archive. Judge freshness by the archive's mtime / size change plus a behavioural re-check, not by the build exit code.
    Root fix: register sa_std/*.sa as input files of the build step.
  • SA_PLUGIN_DEV means opposite things for building and running. Building with it records a Debug configuration (#3); running requires it.
    Root fix: the build ignores this environment variable; the optimisation mode is decided only by -Doptimize.

Judging a run

A run counts as really executed only when all four hold: rc=0; the output contains the expected result lines; the failure name set is empty; dual-route features pass on both routes. rc=0 with an empty log is not a run.

When to clear

  • After any compiler / plugin source change, before running verification.
  • Before canary / gate runs; as the first investigation step when a gate result contradicts the tree.
  • When two copies of the same source behave differently — asymmetric caches are the prime suspect.
  • When an install or rebuild appears to have no effect at all.

Root-fix roadmap (proposal, not implemented)

The commands, variables and behaviours below are proposals; they do not exist in the current toolchain. Goal: the toolchain itself decides whether a cache is stale, instead of relying on human judgement.

1. Toolchain fingerprint in the cache key

Compiler and plugins embed a build-id at build time (for example the git commit + a dirty flag, or the .so hash). Every cache key becomes "source hash + toolchain build-id"; the macro index additionally takes the analyser version. Change the compiler, and the caches invalidate themselves.

Covers: #1, #2, #4, #5, #6. Acceptance: after a plugin rebuild, the first compilation of an unchanged source necessarily misses the cache. Deletable once landed: the "clear everything before verifying" rule, the first three rows of the symptom lookup, and most of cleanup steps 1–3.

2. Unified cache commands

ProposalPurposeReplaces today
sa cache statusList every cache surface's location, size and toolchain build-idRemembering locations and hunting by hand
sa cache clean [--all]One command clears every surface, including .sa_cache outside the plugin treeCleanup steps 0–3
SA_NO_CACHE=1One switch disables all cachesSLA_NO_FRESHNESS_CACHE, which covers only #5
SA_CACHE_TRACE=1On a cache hit, print the cache key and the build-id the artefact came from; staleness stops being "silent"Inferring from symptoms
sa plugin infoShow the installed plugin's build-id, build time and optimisation modemd5 / string grep / .so size

3. Build-side fixes

The "Root fix" items of the traps above: install exit codes, the build ignoring SA_PLUGIN_DEV, the test step really running every time, sa-std-static registering its inputs.

4. Cache-write atomicity to verify

Confirm whether each cache surface writes via "write a temporary file, then rename". If not, an interrupted write leaves a half-written artefact, and parallel tests writing the same cache can overwrite each other — another class of silent error.

Maintenance conventions

  • When a root fix lands, flip the cache table's status column to fixed (version) and note the version on the corresponding trap item.
  • Once the minimum supported version contains the fix, delete the corresponding row, symptom-lookup entry and cleanup step, so this chapter does not only grow.
  • A new cache surface must be documented with all of: location, key (including whether it carries a toolchain version), symptom, cleanup method, status.
